findings.reason: a node following the text either writes a pid it cannot know at publish time or leaves the expiry bound reading a step nobody advances, which is the one mechanism the release rests on.
findings.text: §25 states "The claim's holder fields are written by _publish_launch_claim", but that function runs before the worker exists: it writes claim.json as {"run_id", "claim_registered_at"} (reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:911-914) and its own docstring says "The record carries no pid"; the pid and its start time become known only after _start_supervisor returns (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3527) and are published by attach_launch_identity at dispatch.py:3560, which this change stopped naming at all. So the fields the section requires — and the "step reached" the admit pass is meant to read when deciding expiry — have no writer, and the pass cannot tell a span that has ended from one that has not.

findings.reason: the unit's whole subject is where each read sits relative to the spawn, and an anchor naming the definition's module points the edit at a file the launch span never executes in.
findings.text: the pre-spawn read is specified as "beside _refuse_a_discarded_launch (reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py)", which is the function's definition at dispatch_claims.py:942, while the pre-spawn call it must join is in dispatch.py at :3503 (supervisor branch) and :3507 (launcher branch); the sibling anchor for the second read correctly names the dispatch.py call site, so the two reads are anchored to different kinds of location.

rubric_items.done_when: a finding — case 3 ("claim.json names the pid, host and step reached") measures a file whose only writer runs before the worker exists and emits two fields, so the measure cannot be met by the mechanism the section names.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate logs land "under the run directory" and the refusal lands in the crew home's refusal-traces store (reckon/crew/dispatch_refusals.py:37), both durable paths a later reader can open.
